```{r setup, include = FALSE}

library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.12452> (open access)
* Supplementary Material S1: drug stability analysis, the full description of
  the pharmacodynamic model, the procedure used to reduce the model for the
  simulations, and the NONMEM 7.4 model code. Figures S1-S7: observed and
  predicted time-kill curves for every strain, and the simulations of the
  individual avibactam effects.

```{r citation}
mod_fn <- readModelDb("Chauzy_2019_aztreonam_avibactam")
mod <- rxode2::rxode2(mod_fn)
cat(mod$reference, "\n")
```

Avibactam (AVI) has three effects when combined with aztreonam (ATM): it
inhibits the beta-lactamases that degrade aztreonam, it kills bacteria itself
(through PBP2), and it enhances aztreonam's own killing. Chauzy 2019 fitted one
semi-mechanistic model, jointly, to static time-kill experiments with four
multidrug-resistant, metallo-beta-lactamase-producing Enterobacteriaceae. The
model was fitted to the bacterial counts and to the aztreonam concentrations
measured in the flasks, and the authors then switched the three avibactam
effects on one at a time to measure how much each one contributes.

The packaged model has:

* two bacterial subpopulations with the same logistic growth rate: a
  susceptible `bact_susceptible_susceptible` (P1) and a less-susceptible
  `bact_intermediate_resistant` (P2, a fixed fraction of the inoculum);
* sigmoidal Emax kill by aztreonam on both subpopulations, with the P2 EC50
  multiplied by a resistance factor;
* sigmoidal Emax kill by avibactam on P1 only;
* avibactam enhancement of aztreonam, modelled as a bi-exponential fall in
  the aztreonam EC50, `EC50 = A exp(-alpha AVI) + B exp(-beta AVI)`, which
  applies to both subpopulations;
* aztreonam (`central`, mg/L) degraded first-order at the rate
  `Degmin exp(psi log10(P1 + P2))`, inhibited by avibactam through a
  fractional inhibitory Emax term. There is no degradation sub-model for
  *E. coli* 1266865, because no degradation was observed for it;
* two observations: `log_cfu` (log10 CFU/mL, additive error) and `Cc`
  (aztreonam, mg/L, proportional error), with strain-specific residual SDs.

Aztreonam is added at time 0 as a dose into `central`, with `amt` in mg/L.
Avibactam is the static covariate `CONC_AVI_MGL`. The strain is selected by
`BACT`, which takes the authors' STRAIN codes (1, 12, 15 or 16).

# Population (biological context)

```{r population}
str(mod$population[c("species", "n_subjects", "initial_inoculum", "dose_range")])
```

```{r strains}
strains <- tibble::tribble(
  ~BACT, ~strain, ~beta_lactamases, ~mic_atm, ~mic_atm_avi, ~mic_avi,
  1, "E. coli 1266865", "NDM-5, TEM-OSBL(b), CMY-42", 32, 4, 16,
  12, "C. freundii 974673", "NDM-1, SHV-12(2be), TEM-OSBL(2b), CTX-M-3, CMY-34", 512, 0.125, 16,
  15, "E. cloacae 1285905", "NDM-1, CTX-M-15", 64, 0.25, 32,
  16, "E. cloacae 1318536", "NDM-1, CTX-M-15", 512, 0.125, 16
)
strains |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Strain" = strain,
    "Beta-lactamases" = beta_lactamases,
    "MIC ATM (mg/L)" = mic_atm,
    "MIC ATM + 4 mg/L AVI (mg/L)" = mic_atm_avi,
    "MIC AVI (mg/L)" = mic_avi
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "The four strains (Chauzy 2019 Table 1).")
```

The isolates came from International Health Management Associates. All four
were resistant to aztreonam alone and made susceptible by 4 mg/L avibactam.
Static time-kill experiments ran for 27 h at 37 degrees C in 20 mL
cation-adjusted Mueller-Hinton broth from an inoculum of about 1.5 x 10^6
CFU/mL. Each strain had 32 conditions: a growth control, 6 avibactam-alone
levels, 5 aztreonam-alone levels and 20 combinations, each at least in
duplicate. Counts were plated at 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 15, 21, 24 and 27 h, with
a lower limit of quantification of 200 CFU/mL. Aztreonam was measured by
LC-MS/MS.

# Source trace

| Element | Source location | In the model file |
|---|---|---|
| Logistic growth of P1 + P2, same rate constant | S1 Pharmacodynamic model; code `PLAT`, `DADT(1)`, `DADT(2)` | `kg_s*`, `log10bmax` |
| Inoculum split into P1 and P2 | Table 2 'P2 fraction'; code `A_0(1)`, `A_0(2)`, `MUT` | `log10inoc`, `fmut_s*` |
| Aztreonam sigmoidal Emax on P1 and P2 (P2 EC50 x resistance factor) | code `ATMS`, `ATMR` | `emax_atm_s*`, `hill_atm_s*`, `resfac_s*` |
| Avibactam sigmoidal Emax on P1 only | code `AVIS`, `DADT(1)` | `emax_avi_s*`, `ec50_avi_s*`, `hill_avi_s*` |
| Bi-exponential aztreonam EC50 (enhancement) | S1 Eq 3; code `EC501` | `ec50a_atm_s*`, `ec50b_atm_s*`, `alpha_s*`, `beta_s*` |
| Aztreonam degradation and its inhibition by avibactam | S1 Eq 4; code `NB`, `DEG`, `INH`, `DADT(3)` | `degmin_s*`, `psi_s*`, `ic50_avi_s*`, `hill_inh_s*` |
| No degradation for *E. coli* 1266865 | Table 2 '-'; code `IF(STRAIN.EQ.1) TVDEGMIN = 0` | `degmin_s1 = fixed(0)` |
| Observations and residual error | code `$ERROR` (`IPRD1 = LOG10(ATOT+0.000001)`, `SIG`, `W`) | `log_cfu ~ add()`, `Cc ~ prop()` |
| All parameter values | Table 2; identical to code `$THETA` 1-66 | `ini()` |

The model code in Supplementary Material S1 is the authors' final control
stream: its `$THETA` initial values equal the Table 2 estimates to the printed
digits.

# Parameter table (paper vs. file)

Table 2 is transcribed below and compared with the values read from the
packaged model's `ini()`. This checks the transcription of every parameter.

```{r table2}
table2 <- read.csv(text = "
parameter,s1,s12,s15,s16
kg,0.907,1.1,1.15,1.24
emax_atm,2.62,1.76,1.6,1.86
ec50a_atm,31.8,99.1,2.94,67.9
ec50b_atm,0,0.494,0.241,0.402
alpha,0.42,37.2,25.9,42.3
beta,0,0.548,0.602,0.412
hill_atm,1.48,1.42,2.65,1.52
resfac,8.09,9.39,18,29.1
emax_avi,2.28,1.29,1.69,2.14
ec50_avi,14.5,17.3,14.8,12
hill_avi,12.9,4.63,2.1,8.91
degmin,0,0.00462,0.000129,0.000166
psi,1,0.563,1,1
ic50_avi,1,0.0000213,0.000185,0.0128
hill_inh,1,0.207,0.522,1.48
fmut,0.00001,0.00001,0.00002,0.0000001
addSd_log_cfu,0.97,0.708,0.845,0.782
propSd,0.101,0.494,0.244,0.333
")
theta <- mod$theta
file_vals <- table2 |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-parameter, names_to = "strain", values_to = "paper") |>
  dplyr::mutate(file = unname(theta[paste0(parameter, "_", strain)]))
stopifnot(
  !anyNA(file_vals$file),
  isTRUE(all.equal(file_vals$file, file_vals$paper, tolerance = 1e-12))
)
stopifnot(
  isTRUE(all.equal(unname(theta["log10bmax"]), 8.44)),
  isTRUE(all.equal(unname(theta["log10inoc"]), 6.01))
)
file_vals |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = strain, values_from = c(paper, file)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Table 2 (paper) vs. ini() (file), per strain code. Shared: Nmax 8.44 and INOC 6.01 log10 CFU/mL.")
```

For *E. coli* 1266865, Table 2 prints '-' for the four degradation parameters.
The values 0 / 1 / 1 / 1 in the table above are the constants the authors'
code assigns to STRAIN 1. With `Degmin = 0` the other three have no effect.

# Simulation helper

A time-kill experiment is one flask: aztreonam dosed at time 0 and avibactam
held constant. The model declares two endpoints, so the observation rows set
`dvid = 1`. This returns every model variable, including `log_cfu` and `Cc`.

```{r helper}
sim_flask <- function(bact, atm, avi, times, params = NULL) {
  obs <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = times, evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  ev <- if (atm > 0) {
    rbind(data.frame(id = 1L, time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = atm, cmt = "central", dvid = NA_integer_), obs)
  } else {
    obs
  }
  ev$BACT <- bact
  ev$CONC_AVI_MGL <- avi
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev, params = params, returnType = "data.frame")
  out <- out[out$time %in% times & !duplicated(out$time), c("time", "log_cfu", "Cc")]
  out$BACT <- bact
  out$atm <- atm
  out$avi <- avi
  out
}

fine_times <- seq(0, 27, by = 0.25)
```

# Replicate Figure 2: E. cloacae 1285905 time-kill curves and aztreonam degradation

Figure 2 shows the model fit to *E. cloacae* 1285905 (MIC of aztreonam alone
64 mg/L): (a) aztreonam alone at 16-256 mg/L (0.25-4 x MIC), (b) avibactam
alone, and (c) combinations. The lower panels show the percentage of the
initial aztreonam concentration that remains.

```{r figure-2}
fig2_conds <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(panel = "a: ATM alone", atm = c(16, 32, 64, 128, 256), avi = 0),
  tibble::tibble(panel = "b: AVI alone", atm = 0, avi = c(0.004, 0.0625, 0.5, 4, 32, 64)),
  tibble::tibble(panel = "c: ATM 1 mg/L + AVI", atm = 1, avi = c(0.004, 0.0625, 0.5, 4)),
  tibble::tibble(panel = "c: ATM 8 mg/L + AVI", atm = 8, avi = c(0.004, 0.0625)),
  tibble::tibble(panel = "c: ATM 32 mg/L + AVI", atm = 32, avi = 0.004)
)
fig2 <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(fig2_conds)), function(i) {
  out <- sim_flask(15, fig2_conds$atm[i], fig2_conds$avi[i], fine_times)
  out$panel <- fig2_conds$panel[i]
  out
})) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    condition = ifelse(panel == "b: AVI alone", paste("AVI", avi, "mg/L"),
      ifelse(avi > 0, paste("AVI", avi, "mg/L"), paste("ATM", atm, "mg/L"))
    ),
    atm_remaining_pct = ifelse(atm > 0, 100 * Cc / atm, NA_real_)
  )

ggplot(fig2, aes(time, log_cfu, colour = condition)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = log10(200), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  facet_wrap(~panel, nrow = 2) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 10)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "E. cloacae 1285905 (log10 CFU/mL)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates the model-predicted lines of Figure 2 (top panels) of Chauzy 2019."
  )

fig2 |>
  dplyr::filter(atm > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, atm_remaining_pct, colour = condition)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~panel, nrow = 2) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 120)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "ATM remaining (%)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates the model-predicted lines of Figure 2 (bottom panels) of Chauzy 2019."
  )
```

The behaviour in Figure 2 is reproduced. With aztreonam alone, the two lowest
concentrations let the culture regrow, and aztreonam is then degraded within
about a day. At 128-256 mg/L the culture is killed and about three quarters of
the aztreonam remains at 24 h. Avibactam alone kills only at 32-64 mg/L. When
the counts stay low the degradation stops, which is why aztreonam degradation
depends on the bacterial density.

```{r figure-2-checks}
at <- function(d, panel_, cond_, t_) d$log_cfu[d$panel == panel_ & d$condition == cond_ & d$time == t_]
rem <- function(d, panel_, cond_, t_) d$atm_remaining_pct[d$panel == panel_ & d$condition == cond_ & d$time == t_]
fig2_checks <- c(
  atm16_regrows_by_15h = at(fig2, "a: ATM alone", "ATM 16 mg/L", 15) > 7.5,
  atm16_degraded_by_24h = rem(fig2, "a: ATM alone", "ATM 16 mg/L", 24) < 10,
  atm256_kills_by_15h = at(fig2, "a: ATM alone", "ATM 256 mg/L", 15) < 4,
  atm256_mostly_intact_24h = rem(fig2, "a: ATM alone", "ATM 256 mg/L", 24) > 50,
  avi64_below_inoculum_at_8h = at(fig2, "b: AVI alone", "AVI 64 mg/L", 8) < 5.8,
  avi4_no_kill_at_8h = at(fig2, "b: AVI alone", "AVI 4 mg/L", 8) > 7.5,
  atm32_avi0004_half_left_24h = abs(rem(fig2, "c: ATM 32 mg/L + AVI", "AVI 0.004 mg/L", 24) - 55) < 15,
  atm8_avi00625_protected_24h = rem(fig2, "c: ATM 8 mg/L + AVI", "AVI 0.0625 mg/L", 24) > 70
)
fig2_checks
stopifnot(all(fig2_checks))
```

These checks are figure-level statements read from the model-predicted lines
of Figure 2, with wide margins. The model is deterministic, so they do not
depend on a random seed. Avibactam at 64 mg/L brings the count down only to
about 5 log10 CFU/mL by 8 h, as the fitted line does in Figure 2b. The observed
counts went lower (about 3.7). The model's floor is the less-susceptible P2
subpopulation, which avibactam does not kill and which regrows from about
20 CFU/mL.

# Replicate Figures 4, 5 and S5-S7: contribution of each avibactam effect

The authors simulated constant concentrations at three levels: average
(25 mg/L aztreonam + 4.5 mg/L avibactam), low (5 + 0.9) and high
(125 + 22.5). They used the full model and four reduced models (Supplementary
Material S1, Simulations):

| Scenario | Aztreonam EC50 | Avibactam kill | Degradation inhibited |
|---|---|---|---|
| Full model | `A exp(-alpha AVI) + B exp(-beta AVI)` | yes | yes |
| ATM effect | `A + B` | no | no |
| ATM + AVI inhibitory effect | `A + B` | no | yes |
| ATM + AVI bactericidal effect | `A + B` | yes | no |
| ATM + AVI enhancing effect | `A exp(-alpha AVI) + B exp(-beta AVI)` | no | no |

Each reduced model is the packaged model with parameter overrides: the
enhancement is removed with `alpha = beta = 0`, the avibactam kill with
`Emax,AVI = 0`, and the inhibition of degradation with an IC50 of 1e30 mg/L.

```{r reduced-models}
scenario_params <- function(bact, scenario) {
  s <- paste0("_s", bact)
  no_enh <- setNames(c(0, 0), paste0(c("alpha", "beta"), s))
  no_kill <- setNames(0, paste0("emax_avi", s))
  no_inh <- setNames(1e30, paste0("ic50_avi", s))
  switch(scenario,
    "Full model" = NULL,
    "ATM effect" = c(no_enh, no_kill, no_inh),
    "ATM + AVI inhibitory" = c(no_enh, no_kill),
    "ATM + AVI bactericidal" = c(no_enh, no_inh),
    "ATM + AVI enhancing" = c(no_kill, no_inh)
  )
}
scenarios <- c("Full model", "ATM effect", "ATM + AVI inhibitory", "ATM + AVI bactericidal", "ATM + AVI enhancing")
levels_conc <- tibble::tibble(
  level = c("average", "low", "high"),
  atm = c(25, 5, 125),
  avi = c(4.5, 0.9, 22.5)
)
sim_grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(BACT = strains$BACT, level = levels_conc$level, scenario = c("Control", scenarios)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(levels_conc, by = "level")
effects <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(sim_grid)), function(i) {
  g <- sim_grid[i, ]
  if (g$scenario == "Control") {
    out <- sim_flask(g$BACT, 0, 0, fine_times)
  } else {
    out <- sim_flask(g$BACT, g$atm, g$avi, fine_times, params = scenario_params(g$BACT, g$scenario))
  }
  out$level <- g$level
  out$scenario <- g$scenario
  out
})) |>
  dplyr::left_join(strains |> dplyr::select(BACT, strain), by = "BACT")
```

```{r figure-s5, fig.height = 8}
effects |>
  dplyr::filter(level == "average", time <= 24) |>
  dplyr::mutate(scenario = factor(scenario, levels = c("Control", scenarios))) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, log_cfu, colour = scenario)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = log10(200), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  facet_grid(strain ~ scenario) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 9)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 12, 24)) +
  theme(legend.position = "none", strip.text = element_text(size = 7)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Bacterial count (log10 CFU/mL)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure S5 (and Figures 4 and 5, top panels) of Chauzy 2019: 25 mg/L ATM + 4.5 mg/L AVI.\nThe Control column is the drug-free growth curve (0% effect)."
  )
```

```{r figure-5-atm}
effects |>
  dplyr::filter(level == "average", BACT == 15, scenario %in% scenarios, time <= 24) |>
  dplyr::mutate(scenario = factor(scenario, levels = scenarios)) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Cc)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~scenario, nrow = 1) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 26)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "ATM concentration (mg/L)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 5 (bottom panels) of Chauzy 2019: E. cloacae 1285905, 25 mg/L ATM + 4.5 mg/L AVI."
  )
```

As in Figure 5, aztreonam stays at 25 mg/L under the full model. It falls to
about 0 by 21 h when neither the avibactam inhibition nor its enhancement is
present, because the culture regrows and degrades the drug. With the
enhancement alone it levels off near 19 mg/L. Kill is slower, so some
degradation happens before the culture is controlled.

## Percentage of the maximum effect

The paper defines the effect of each scenario from the area under the log10
CFU-time curve, `AUC_CFU`:

`% maximum effect = 100 (AUC_CFU,control - AUC_CFU,i) / (AUC_CFU,control - AUC_CFU,full)`

The paper does not say how `AUC_CFU` was computed. The published curves are
piecewise linear between the experiment's sampling times (0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10,
15, 21 and 24 h), so the AUC is taken here with the linear trapezoidal rule on
those times, from 0 to 24 h. The paper's figures also plot the log10 count
only down to 0 (1 CFU/mL). Reading the AUC on that floor reproduces every
published percentage. Without the floor, the high-concentration values fall
well below the published ones, because the full model then goes as low as
-6 log10 CFU/mL and the denominator grows. Both readings are shown below. The
floored one is the one checked.

```{r pct-max-effect}
sampling_times <- c(0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 15, 21, 24)
auc_trap <- function(t, y) sum(diff(t) * (head(y, -1) + tail(y, -1)) / 2)
auc_tab <- effects |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% sampling_times) |>
  dplyr::group_by(BACT, strain, level, scenario) |>
  dplyr::arrange(time, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    auc_floor0 = auc_trap(time, pmax(log_cfu, 0)),
    auc_nofloor = auc_trap(time, log_cfu),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
pct_tab <- auc_tab |>
  dplyr::filter(!scenario %in% c("Control", "Full model")) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    auc_tab |> dplyr::filter(scenario == "Control") |> dplyr::select(BACT, level, ctrl0 = auc_floor0, ctrln = auc_nofloor),
    by = c("BACT", "level")
  ) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    auc_tab |> dplyr::filter(scenario == "Full model") |> dplyr::select(BACT, level, full0 = auc_floor0, fulln = auc_nofloor),
    by = c("BACT", "level")
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    pct_floor0 = 100 * (ctrl0 - auc_floor0) / (ctrl0 - full0),
    pct_nofloor = 100 * (ctrln - auc_nofloor) / (ctrln - fulln)
  )

cmp <- published |>
  dplyr::left_join(pct_tab |> dplyr::select(BACT, strain, level, scenario, pct_floor0, pct_nofloor),
    by = c("BACT", "level", "scenario")
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    diff_pp = pct_floor0 - published,
    level = factor(level, levels = c("low", "average", "high"))
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(level, BACT)
stopifnot(nrow(cmp) == 48, !anyNA(cmp$pct_floor0))

cmp |>
  dplyr::select(level, strain, scenario, published, pct_floor0, pct_nofloor, diff_pp) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Concentration level" = level,
    "Strain" = strain,
    "Scenario" = scenario,
    "Published (%)" = published,
    "Simulated, AUC floored at 0 (%)" = pct_floor0,
    "Simulated, no floor (%)" = pct_nofloor,
    "Difference, floored - published (percentage points)" = diff_pp
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Percentage of the maximum effect: Figures S5 (average), S6 (low) and S7 (high) of Chauzy 2019 vs. the packaged model.")
```

```{r pct-max-effect-checks}
summary(abs(cmp$diff_pp))
# Deterministic comparison against the printed figure labels. The largest
# difference observed is about 2.7 percentage points (E. coli 1266865 at the
# high level); a mis-transcribed parameter moves these by tens of points.
stopifnot(max(abs(cmp$diff_pp)) < 5)

# The paper's main conclusion: at clinical average and low concentrations the
# enhancing effect alone gives most of the full effect (82.5-100%), while the
# inhibition of degradation adds little to aztreonam alone.
enh <- cmp |> dplyr::filter(level != "high", scenario == "ATM + AVI enhancing")
stopifnot(all(enh$pct_floor0 > 80))
inh_gain <- cmp |>
  dplyr::filter(scenario %in% c("ATM effect", "ATM + AVI inhibitory")) |>
  dplyr::select(BACT, level, scenario, pct_floor0) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = scenario, values_from = pct_floor0) |>
  dplyr::mutate(gain = `ATM + AVI inhibitory` - `ATM effect`)
stopifnot(all(inh_gain$gain < 10))
```

The model reproduces all 48 published percentages within a few percentage
points, and it reproduces the paper's conclusion. Within the clinical
concentration range, the enhancement of aztreonam explains nearly all of the
combined activity. Inhibiting aztreonam degradation adds at most a few
percentage points over aztreonam alone.

# Why there is no PKNCA section

This is a pharmacodynamic model of a closed in vitro flask. Aztreonam enters as
one addition at time 0 and is lost only by enzymatic degradation, which depends
on the bacteria. Avibactam is held constant. There is no dosing regimen or
systemic exposure for NCA to summarise, so the validation above compares the
model with the paper's own model predictions: the time-kill and degradation
profiles of Figure 2, and the percentages of the maximum effect in Figures 4,
5 and S5-S7.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **One joint model, strain selected by `BACT`.** The authors fitted all four
  strains in one NONMEM run, sharing Nmax and the inoculum. The file therefore
  holds the full set of strain-specific parameters and switches on the
  dataset's STRAIN codes (1, 12, 15, 16), which are kept as the `BACT` levels.
  Any other `BACT` value returns NA.
* **No random effects.** `$OMEGA` on the growth rate is fixed to 0 in the
  published code, so no between-flask variability is included. The residual SDs
  are THETAs with `$SIGMA 1 FIX`, so the strain-specific Table 2 values are
  SDs. They are selected per strain in `model()`.
* **Units of `Degmin` and `psi`.** Table 2 gives Degmin in 1/h, and Supplementary
  Material S1 gives it in mg/L/h. The code multiplies Degmin by the aztreonam
  amount (`DADT(3) = -(DEG*INH)*A(3)`), so it is a first-order rate constant in
  1/h. Table 2 gives psi in mL/CFU, but the code multiplies it by
  `NB = LOG10(A(1)+A(2))`, the log10 of the count. The file follows the code and
  labels psi per log10 CFU/mL.
* **Degradation parameters for *E. coli* 1266865.** Table 2 prints '-'. The code
  sets Degmin = 0 and psi, IC50 and the inhibition Hill coefficient to 1 for
  this strain. The same constants are used here, fixed. They have no effect.
* **Numerical guards.** At high concentrations a fully killed culture can reach a
  tiny negative count through solver error. The count is floored at a small
  positive value inside the `log10()` of the degradation term, and at 0 before
  the code's 1e-6 CFU/mL offset in `log_cfu`. Neither guard changes any
  positive-count value.
* **Censoring.** Counts below 200 CFU/mL were handled with the M3 method in the
  fit. This is a data-handling choice, not part of the structural model, and it
  is not in the file.
* **How `AUC_CFU` was computed.** This was not stated in the paper. The
  maintainers used the linear trapezoidal rule from 0 to 24 h on the sampling
  times, with the log10 count floored at 0. With that reading all 48 published
  percentages are reproduced. The floor matters only when the full model kills
  far below 1 CFU/mL, which happens at the high concentrations.
* **Errata.** The PubMed record (PMID 31420947) links no correction, and the
  PMC full text carries no correction notice (checked 2026-11-26).
